Illinois Computing Accelerator for Non-Specialists (iCAN) Goal: Expand the iCAN program to 20-25 students in 2021 with at least 50% of enrolled students identifying as underrepresented in computing because of their race, gender, and/or disability status.
Activities: To broaden access to computing for people with a bachelor’s degree in any field other than CS, we created iCAN, which launched in the fall of 2020. iCAN’s mission is to broaden participation in computing through an accelerated program for non-CS college graduates.
The inaugural class has 7 students, 57% of whom are from groups underrepresented in computing because of their gender and/or race.
We seek to expand to 20-25 students, and apply to enable students to be eligible for federal student loans to make the program more accessible (Williams, Amato, Viswanathan).
Collect and Analyze Data: Retention Goal: In 2020-2021, identify rates of attrition among CS majors to guide our 2021-2022 BPC Plan.

Activities: To better understand attrition within our BS programs, we will identify our attrition rates disaggregated by race, ethnicity, gender, and first-generation college status (Chacko).
These data will inform the BPC plan for 2021-2022, but will not necessarily be shared.
Collect and Analyze Data: Data Buddies Survey Goal: In 2020-2021, expand student participation in the Data Buddies Survey to at least 500 undergraduate students and 300 graduate students. (Previously 172 and 176, respectively).
Activities: To better understand our students’ experiences, we seek to increase our student’s participation in the annual Data Buddies survey, which disaggregates data by gender and race.
We plan to (1) offer a raffle (Lewis), (2) promote the survey with our student groups (Coleman), (3) share email and presentation templates with faculty (Amato), and (4) promote the survey in weekly department emails that students receive (Harris).
In the Spring of 2021, we will review our Data Buddies Survey report in a departmental faculty meeting.
Student Community Organization Goal: Provide student organizations transparency into and a voice in departmental BPC efforts.

Activities: To have students’ priorities drive our BPC efforts, we have student representation on our BPC committee and we will solicit suggestions of BPC initiatives at the monthly CS Student Leadership Council (CSSLC) meetings (Coleman/Amato/Harris).
We have a thriving set of student organizations that are represented at the CSSLC meetings (e.g., Blacks and African Americans in Computing, Latinxs in Computer Science, Women in Computer Science, WiCyS, AI4ALL, and Hack4Impact).
At the CSSLC meetings, students will also be encouraged to attend the Department Head’s weekly open office hours to share additional suggestions.
To provide transparency to students, we will also present updates from the BPC committee with particular attention to how student suggestions have shaped the committee’s work.
Faculty and Staff BPC Education Goal: Encourage faculty and staff participation in opportunities to learn about BPC and racism.
Activities: To increase faculty and staff knowledge of BPC and racism more generally, we will encourage participation in relevant workshops and seminars.
Faculty will be asked to report their participation in their annual faculty reports.

In the fall of 2020, we started the monthly speaker series “Illinois Computer Science Conversations on Equity & Justice in Computing.” This supplements workshops and seminars hosted by the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion and the Grainger College of Engineering Institute for Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access.
We will promote at least one event in each “Inside CS Weekly Digest” (Harris).

Levine <​josh@email.arizona.edu​>, Associate Professor and Director of DEI Context University of Arizona (UA) is one of three major public universities in the state of Arizona.
UA is one of only a few R1 research universities to be a Hispanic Serving Institution, and the first of the three AZ state universities to have that distinction.
The Department of Computer Science (UACS) serves approximately 1400 undergrads and 100 graduate students.
